beforeEvidence: Open the stall, my dear. Let the people come.
Watch what they ask for. I will see you tonight.
afterEvidence: Did you buy for the people who came, or the people you imagined?
If you forget what we said, it is written in your Notebook.
duringPricing: Go to the price board by your stall, my dear. Try a price, and watch who walks away.
I will come by when you have tried a few.
afterPricing: Too high and they walk. Too low and you work for nothing. Where is your price today?
It is all in your Notebook.

lines: Welcome to the market, my dear. I am Maame Gyasiwaa. I have sold from this corner for thirty years.
Buy your stock, open your stall, and let the people come. Watch what they ask for.
Tonight, when you have counted your takings, I will come and see how you did.
The goals on the left are yours. Finish them, and I will show you the next step.
Your Notebook is at the top right. I will help you fill it.
Ei, my dear. I watched your stall all day.

lines.text: {missedPeople} asked for {missedItem} and you had none. They did not wait. They walked on.
Your shelf and your customers matched today. Tell me, was that planning, or luck?

lines: You chose what to buy before anyone told you what they wanted. That was a guess. There is no shame in a guess.
But a guess is not knowing. Your customers tell you what they want every day, if you watch them.
Tomorrow, buy for the people who come, not the people you imagine. I have written it in your Notebook.
Well done, my dear. You can read your customers now. Next question: what do you charge them?
There is a price board beside your stall. Go and set your own prices.
Raise a price and some people will walk away. Lower it and more will buy, but you keep less from each one.
Try something. Then watch what happens.
Ei, my dear. I saw you at the price board today.

lines.text: {pricedPeople} looked at your price for {pricedItem} and walked away.
You sold {lossItem} for less than it cost you. You lost {lossAmount} on every one. Customers love that. Your purse does not.
You sold {thinCount} {thinItem}, but you keep only {thinProfit} from each. Plenty of work for very little.
Nobody walked away and your margins were fair. Now try a little higher, and see how far people will go.

lines: You took in {revenueToday} today. But after paying for the goods, you kept {profitToday}. That is the money that is yours.
Money coming in is not money kept. Revenue is what comes in. Profit is what stays.
A price is a guess about what people will pay. Test it, the way you tested what they wanted.
I have written it in your Notebook.
